subject: Committed spend drawdown: proposed ramped burn & replenishment model
messages:

Cc: Elena Morales <elena@greenstack.io>, GreenStack Procurement <procurement@greenstack.io>

Subject: Re: Committed spend discussion — drawdown questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the proposal deck. Procurement had a couple of follow-ups around the wallet/drawdown mechanics before we send this to finance:

- Can you confirm whether unused credits can roll between months inside a year, and whether any credits expire at year-end?
- We need a clear replenishment trigger: do you auto-replenish to a fixed top-up once the wallet falls below X%?
- How do discounts scale if we ramp spend across years? GreenStack prefers a model that increases discount as we commit more.

We've attached a simple 6-quarter forecast (attached) to show our expected ramp. Also looped Elena (legal) and procurement mailbox.

Appreciate a quick clarifying note — we want to get this into our procurement review next week.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Morales <elena@greenstack.io>, GreenStack Procurement <procurement@greenstack.io>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Committed spend discussion — drawdown questions

Hannah — thanks for the clear questions and for the forecast, that helps. High level answer and two concrete options we typically offer:

1) Credit behavior and expiry
- Option A (Annual bucket, monthly draw): Credits live in an annual wallet that rolls month-to-month within the same contract year; unused credits at year-end expire unless you elect a 60-day extension window (paid at 20% of unused face value) to move them into year+1.
- Option B (Replenishable wallet): Credits are top-up credits that replenish automatically when the remaining balance dips below a configured threshold (we usually recommend 25% of initial wallet). Replenishments are drawn from a pre-authorized replenishment reserve (invoiced as consumed).

2) Replenishment trigger and mechanics
- Auto top-up (Option B) — when wallet <= 25% we trigger a replenishment equal to 50% of the original wallet. Top-ups can be capped per quarter.
- Manual top-up (Option A) — procurement triggers replenishment PRs; no automatic charge.

3) Discounting across multi-year ramp
- We can structure year-over-year stepped discounts. Example: Year 1 baseline 8% vs on-demand, Year 2 12%, Year 3 16% for increasing committed $ bands. We can make tiers tied to cumulative consumption to allow dynamic step-ups.

4) Accounting and refunds for early termination
- Standard approach: unconsumed, pre-paid balance is refundable pro rata with a 10% administrative fee after 90 days; if credits are non-refundable by contract, we offer a transfer to other BU within your org with permission.

I'll propose language and two sample amortization schedules (frontloaded ramp vs steady monthly) for Dev and Laura to confirm. Attaching a draft term doc with the above options.

Next steps: let me know which option (A or B) you prefer for replenishment and whether GreenStack needs credits to be non-expiring inside the three-year term. I'll update the term sheet accordingly.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi / team — quick legal clarifications:

- If credits are refundable pro rata, we need a 30-day notice window for termination and an audit run-rate reconciliation to compute unconsumed usage.
- The 60-day extension with a 20% fee sounds reasonable as an option, but we would prefer language that allows a one-time carryover per year rather than repeated deferrals.
- Can you confirm how you report token-level consumption for audit (CSV export or S3)? This must align with our internal chargeback reports.

Thanks,
Elena (Legal)

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Committed spend discussion — drawdown questions

Looping in Laura and Dev to confirm accounting and contract language. Responses inline: 

- Audit / reporting: we provide token-level consumption exports daily via S3, and a summarized monthly CSV suitable for chargeback. We'll include a named S3 bucket with read-only credentials for your finance team.
- Carryover policy: we can agree to one one-time year-end carryover per contract year (not stackable) for Option A.
- Refund mechanics: Dev, can you confirm the pro-rata refund calculation and the administrative fee? Also please confirm whether we can support a 30-day termination notice with an audit reconciliation.

Laura — curious if we want to push for a small non-refundable minimum in year 1 if GreenStack wants more carryover flexibility.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Cole <h.cole@greenstack.io>, Elena Morales <elena@greenstack.io>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Committed spend discussion — drawdown questions

Quick finance confirmation:

- Refunds: pro-rata based on remaining gross dollars in the prepaid wallet at termination date, subtracting any outstanding usage invoices. We can apply a standard 10% administrative fee (we can negotiate to 7.5% at scale).
- Audit window: 30 days notice then 14-day reconciliation period (we provide daily usage CSV and a final audit export).
- Invoicing cadence: for multi-year deals we prefer annual upfront invoicing per contract year. If GreenStack prefers quarterly invoicing, we can support quarterly prepay but discount cadence will move to per-quarter tiers (slightly lower effective discount).

Recommended commercial language for the term sheet (sample):
"Upon termination, any unconsumed prepaid balance will be refunded on a pro-rata basis within thirty (30) days of final audit, less a ten percent (10%) administrative fee. Customer is entitled to one (1) one-time carryover of unused credits into the next contract year, provided Customer elects such carryover in writing within sixty (60) days of year-end."

Laura / Rishi: if GreenStack accepts annual upfront invoicing with the stepped discount schedule (8% / 12% / 16%), we can keep the higher discount profile. If they need quarterly invoices, suggest we move to 6% / 9% / 12% respectively.

Dev Patel
Finance Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Committed spend drawdown: proposed ramped burn & replenishment model

Thanks everyone — to summarize and capture a preferred path forward from this thread: 

GreenStack preference (per Hannah): Option B — Replenishable wallet with auto top-up at 25% remaining, replenishment equals 50% of original wallet, capped at one top-up per quarter.
Legal (Elena) asked for: 30-day termination notice, one-time year-end carryover, token-level S3 export for audits — all agreed in principle.
Finance (Dev): annual upfront invoicing keeps the higher stepped discounts (8% / 12% / 16% across three years). Quarterly invoicing is possible but reduces the effective discount (6% / 9% / 12%).

Action items:
- I will update the term sheet to reflect Option B mechanics, auto top-up trigger, and the one-time carryover rule. (Rishi) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Legal / Procurement to review the updated term language for carryover and refund mechanics (Elena / procurement).
- Dev: please prepare the sample invoice language for annual vs quarterly and confirm the accounting memo for recognition.

If there are no major objections, I'll push the updated term sheet to DocuSign and the HubSpot deal record.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
